- When sentiment turns negative or shows sharp decline, reduce forecasted price momentum; avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings.
- If sentiment has been consistently positive over recent days, model should not over-forecast upward; cap upward revisions at 1–2% above recent high unless news volume spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecasted peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is low, model should not ignore the trend — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day to reflect subdued market sentiment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period price increases — cap final 5–7 days of forecast at 1–2% below prior 30-day average to reflect mean reversion.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model should avoid large directional moves — use 1–2% smoothing around recent 7-day average to avoid false momentum.
